Record date: 2129-02-20
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 02/20/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Continued management of COPD, evaluation of renal function, and follow-up on mental health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately five weeks after his last visit. He reports a slight increase in respiratory symptoms, particularly exacerbated by the recent winter weather. He describes episodes of increased shortness of breath, particularly upon exertion, and notes that he has been using his albuterol inhaler more frequently, averaging eight times daily. The productive cough remains, with clear sputum, and he denies any hemoptysis or fever.
Mr. Fairfax continues to experience significant bilateral lower extremity edema, which he rates as 8/10 in discomfort. Despite compliance with the prescribed sodium-restricted diet and furosemide at 200 mg daily, he reports no noticeable improvement, having gained an additional 3 pounds since the last visit. He expresses frustration with the persistent swelling and discomfort.
On the mental health front, Mr. Fairfax states that his anxiety has worsened, particularly related to his ongoing health issues. He reports difficulty sleeping, with frequent awakenings and a sense of restlessness. He has been attending cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions regularly but feels that he may need a medication adjustment.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + weight gain, + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + increased exertional dyspnea, + productive cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using eight times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 200 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.5F, HR 80, BP 138/85, RR 26, O2 sat 82% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued but cooperative. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.8, Hgb 10.2, Hct 30.5, Plt 215. 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.5, Cl 99, CO2 21, BUN 50, Cr 3.0, Glucose 88. 3. BNP: 750 (elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.6 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status has worsened since the last visit, with increased reliance on bronchodilators. A referral to pulmonary medicine is essential for further evaluation of his COPD management plan and possible initiation of a nebulized bronchodilator regimen. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. The serum creatinine has worsened, indicating further renal impairment. Nephrology will be consulted urgently for assessment and management of his renal function. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema remains significant despite diuretic therapy. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and continue furosemide at 200 mg daily. Daily weight monitoring remains essential, and nephrology follow-up will be pursued. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. A referral to psychiatry for medication management will be expedited due to increased anxiety and insomnia. Continued engagement in cognitive-behavioral therapy is encouraged.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
